title: Indexes with Included Columns
description: Learn how to add non-key columns to non-clustered indexes to cover more queries and avoid key lookups.

data.text: SQL Server Indexes with Included Columns

By including non-key columns in non-clustered indexes, you can create nonclustered indexes that cover more queries. When an index contains all the columns referenced by a query, it is called a covering index.
When a non-clustered index does not contain all columns needed by a query, SQL Server performs a key lookup to fetch the missing columns from the clustered index or heap. This can be expensive.

data.title: CREATE INDEX with INCLUDE clause
data.content: Creates a unique index with included columns to avoid key lookups.

data.title: Index with included columns
data.content: Creates an index on email with first_name and last_name included.

data.text: Included columns are stored at the leaf level of the non-clustered index but are not part of the B-tree sort order. That gives them two advantages over key columns: they do not count towards the 900-byte (1,700-byte for non-clustered from SQL Server 2016) key limit, and they do not need to be sorted on every insert. The script below builds a covering index and confirms the key/included split.

data.title: Key column plus included columns
data.content: Only `email` is sorted; `first_name` and `last_name` ride along at the leaf level to satisfy the SELECT list.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE #Customers (
    customer_id INT IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    email NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    first_name NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    last_name  NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ix_cust_email ON #Customers (email)
    INCLUDE (first_name, last_name);

-- Fully covered by the index: no key lookup needed
SELECT email, first_name, last_name
FROM #Customers
WHERE email = N'ada@example.com';

SELECT
    c.name AS column_name,
    ic.is_included_column
FROM tempdb.sys.index_columns AS ic
JOIN tempdb.sys.columns AS c ON c.object_id = ic.object_id AND c.column_id = ic.column_id
WHERE ic.object_id = OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#Customers')
ORDER BY ic.is_included_column, ic.key_ordinal;

data.title: Do not dump every column in the index
data.text: Stuffing all columns into INCLUDE turns the index into a second copy of the table: it doubles storage and slows every write. Include only the columns a specific query needs, and prefer several narrow covering indexes over one wide one.

data.title: Included Columns Key Points
points: Included columns are non-key columns added to a non-clustered index.
They allow the query optimizer to satisfy queries entirely from the index.
This avoids expensive key lookups to the clustered index or heap.
Use INCLUDE for columns frequently selected but not filtered on.
